description: The false-positive block. In every case a repair is *possible* -- the names are close, or the value looks castable -- and the correct answer is to do nothing at all. `expected_payload` is therefore always identical to `payload`. Any applied operation here is a silently wrong repair, which is the failure mode that actually costs users data.

cases.name: opposites_created_vs_updated
cases.description: created_at and updated_at differ by three characters and mean opposite things. Writing a creation timestamp into an update field corrupts an audit trail silently.
cases.known_gap: Uncontested rename: with one missing field and one unexpected key there is no competitor, so margin is 1.0 and trust collapses to raw name similarity (0.752). See the Phase 7 findings -- the must-refuse ceiling (0.923) sits above the must-apply floor (0.809), so no single threshold on name similarity separates these.

cases.name: opposites_min_vs_max_price
cases.description: min_price and max_price share seven of nine characters. Swapping them inverts a filter.
cases.known_gap: Uncontested rename; jaro-winkler 0.867 against a must-apply floor of 0.809. Not separable by threshold.

cases.name: opposites_start_vs_end_date
cases.description: start_date / end_date share the '_date' suffix.

cases.name: opposites_first_vs_last_name
cases.description: first_name / last_name share '_name'. A person's given name in a surname field is wrong data, not drift.
cases.known_gap: Uncontested rename; jaro-winkler 0.826 against a must-apply floor of 0.809. Not separable by threshold.

cases.name: opposites_is_active_vs_is_archived
cases.description: Both boolean, both 'is_a...', opposite meaning.
cases.known_gap: Uncontested rename; jaro-winkler 0.923 -- the worst case in the corpus. Winkler's prefix bonus actively rewards the shared 'is_a' prefix that makes these two opposites look alike.

cases.name: opposites_sender_vs_receiver_id
cases.description: sender_id / receiver_id share the '_id' suffix and the message-routing context.

cases.name: opposites_input_vs_output_path
cases.description: input_path / output_path. Writing the input over the output silently destroys a file.

cases.name: wrong_entity_user_vs_order_id
cases.description: Both are ids; they identify different things.

cases.name: wrong_entity_billing_vs_shipping_city
cases.description: Same field one level down, wrong branch.

cases.name: unrelated_names
cases.description: No plausible correspondence at all -- the easy end of the block.

cases.name: value_word_not_a_number
cases.description: "five" is a number to a human and not to int().

cases.name: value_decimal_string_to_int
cases.description: "5.5" -> 5 would silently discard the fraction.

cases.name: value_superscript_digit
cases.description: '²'.isdigit() is True but int('²') raises. A cast that cannot be performed must not be proposed.

cases.name: value_maybe_is_not_a_boolean
cases.description: Only the four accepted boolean spellings coerce.

cases.name: value_yes_is_not_a_boolean
cases.description: "yes" is conventional English, not a JSON boolean. Accepting it is a slippery slope to accepting "y", "on", "enabled".

cases.name: value_nan_string
cases.description: float("nan") succeeds, NaN poisons every downstream comparison, and it is not valid JSON.

cases.name: value_infinity_string
cases.description: Same argument as NaN.

cases.name: json_scalar_where_object_expected
cases.description: "123" is valid JSON but parses to an int, not an object.

cases.name: json_array_where_object_expected
cases.description: Parsing succeeds but yields the wrong kind.

cases.name: json_duplicate_key
cases.description: json.loads keeps the last duplicate silently. There is no fidelity score that honestly describes 'one of these two values is gone'.

cases.name: json_array_wrong_item_types
cases.description: The string parses to an array, but its elements do not match the declared item_type.

cases.name: array_item_type_mismatch
cases.description: One bad element in an otherwise valid array is an item-level problem no cast fixes.

cases.name: untyped_array_not_wrapped
cases.description: Wrapping into an array with no declared item_type is a guess about cardinality with nothing to check it against.

cases.name: enum_near_miss_typo
cases.description: 'in progres' is one character from a member. Levenshtein over enum values is a different and riskier feature than normalising spelling.

cases.name: enum_value_not_a_member
cases.description: 'cancelled' is a perfectly reasonable status that this contract does not declare.

cases.name: enum_separator_removed_not_mapped
cases.description: 'onhold' is not 'on_hold' -- enum values are data, and collapsing separators entirely claims a member on thinner evidence than normalisation warrants.

cases.name: enum_int_out_of_range
cases.description: An integer enum given a value outside the set. Normalisation is a string operation and has nothing to offer.

cases.name: enum_declared_as_a_bare_string
cases.description: A malformed schema: tuple('open') splits into characters, so 'O' would match member 'o'. Refusing beats rewriting data because the schema was wrong.

cases.name: root_multi_element_array
cases.description: Two objects at the root: no principled element to pick.

cases.name: root_bare_scalar
cases.description: A single-field contract makes {city: 'Mumbai'} a plausible reading, but it is an inference about intent rather than a re-encoding of structured data.

cases.name: root_empty_list
cases.description: Recovering an object from [] would mean fabricating one.

cases.name: object_where_scalar_expected
cases.description: A dict for a float field. Nothing safe to do.

cases.name: null_where_value_expected
cases.description: An explicit null is a deliberate value, not a missing field to fill.

cases.name: missing_field_with_no_default
cases.description: Nothing declares what this field should be, and nothing in the payload resembles it.

cases.name: int_in_a_float_field_needs_no_repair
cases.description: An int is already acceptable where a float is declared, so there is no violation and nothing to coerce. The int->float cast exists for union members; firing it here would be a no-op the audit trail should not claim.
